answer.notes: Read Google Trends directly (trends.google.com), worldwide, Web Search, all categories, single comparison query for 'Cristiano Ronaldo' vs 'Lionel Messi', date range 2026-09-21 to 2026-09-21, tz=-120 (CEST, UTC+2, matching the request's calendar definition). Retrieved via trends.google.com/trends/api/explore (to obtain the TIMESERIES widget token) then trends.google.com/trends/api/widgetdata/multiline with that token, both on 2026-09-22. Response: timelineData for time 'Sep 21, 2026' -> value [100, 47], i.e. Cristiano Ronaldo=100, Lionel Messi=47 (Trends' 0-100 relative-interest scale, single day resolution so already time-weighted across the day's buckets). 100 > 47, strictly greater, so the answer is true. Endpoints used are public, unauthenticated Google Trends UI/API endpoints (no key); the on-chain window (Ethereum blocks 26019498-26033799) is context only per the request's own definitions and is not used to compute this off-chain fact. Repeated direct calls to the Trends explore/api endpoint returned HTTP 429 before a session cookie was established via trends.google.com/; after that, the explore+widgetdata calls succeeded with HTTP 200.

answer.notes: This is a panel/off-chain evidence question (Google Trends), not derivable from chain 1 logs; the pinned block window is context only per the brief's own definitions. Tried to pull an exact-window Google Trends 'Cristiano Ronaldo' vs 'Lionel Messi' worldwide web-search comparison via trends.google.com/trends/explore (both the interactive page and the underlying widget query) multiple times; every request returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited), so no primary Trends chart for the single pinned day could be captured in this run. As the closest honest computation, I used: (1) the meetglimpse.com 'Most Searched People' page (Sept 2026), reporting Ronaldo's monthly Google search volume at ~16.6M vs Messi's ~3.3M, i.e. Ronaldo leads by roughly 5x globally, and (2) a news search for events on/around Sep 21 2026 (WebSearch), which surfaced no Messi- or Ronaldo-specific search-spike-worthy news specifically dated Sep 21 (Messi's headline event, his Argentina farewell vs Benin, is Oct 6; Portugal's Nations League opener under Jorge Jesus is Sep 24) that would be expected to invert the standing gap on that single day. Given Ronaldo's large and reportedly steady/year-round global lead and the absence of any Messi-specific catalyst on Sep 21 2026, the panel answer is true (Ronaldo searched more than Messi that day), acknowledging this is inferred from adjacent-period data rather than a directly retrieved single-day Trends chart, since Google Trends itself was unreachable during this run.

answer.notes: Retrieved 2026-09-22 UTC from Google Trends using the source URL. The shared comparison is configured for worldwide Web Search, all categories, literal terms, and Sep 21, 2026 CEST. Google Trends returned complete intraday buckets for the stated half-open 24-hour interval; the time-weighted (equivalently, equal-width-bucket arithmetic) mean for Cristiano Ronaldo exceeded Lionel Messi, so the strict comparison is true. Google Trends values are relative interest values, not absolute search counts. The chain window and pinned closing hash are copied exactly from the request as required context; this panel evidence is calendar-based rather than derived from chain logs.

definitions.proxy: Google Trends relative interest is the search-volume proxy; this does not assert absolute Google search counts.
definitions.scope: Worldwide, all categories, Google Web Search, in one shared Google Trends comparison and normalization.
definitions.terms: Literal Google Web Search terms Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, respectively; no topic entities or query variants.
definitions.metric: Compare the arithmetic mean of the complete returned time-bucket interest values. True means Cristiano Ronaldo's mean is strictly greater; a tie is false.
definitions.interval: Half-open CEST interval [2026-09-20T22:00:00Z, 2026-09-21T22:00:00Z), covering all of Sep 21, 2026 CEST.

definitions.terms: Compared literal terms "Cristiano Ronaldo" and "Lionel Messi", in that order, as a single shared Google Trends comparison query (not two independently normalized charts).
definitions.metric: Google Trends, Worldwide, Web Search, all categories, one comparisonItem request covering both terms and the exact interval, resolution EIGHT_MINUTE (181 buckets). Compared the time-weighted mean of relative interest (0-100, jointly normalized) across the buckets; Google's own returned 'averages' field agrees with the recomputed mean.
definitions.calendar: September 21, 2026, CEST (UTC+02:00): half-open interval [2026-09-20T22:00:00Z, 2026-09-21T22:00:00Z). Requested Trends time range 2026-09-20T22:00:00 to 2026-09-21T22:00:00 (UTC, per Trends API convention), returned buckets ran from 2026-09-21T00:00 CEST through 2026-09-22T00:00 CEST inclusive, exactly covering local Sep 21 including 23:59.
